Reference key: apply_mint_gate — global gating ratio vs per-(node, agent) breakdown

WHAT THE QUESTION ASKS
The final step of apply_mint_gate re-derives per-agent mint after gating the per-node mint. The comment block just above that step states the tradeoff explicitly and states the choice made.

THE EXPLICIT TRADEOFF (precision vs available data)
- Available data: The function does NOT have a per-(node, agent) breakdown of mint. It only has:
  - node_mint_orig (per-node mint, original) and gated_node_mint (per-node mint after gating), and
  - agent_mint_orig (per-agent attribution, original).
  There is no record of how much each agent's mint came from each specific node, so a precise per-node re-attribution of each agent's share is not possible with the data on hand.
- Precision cost: Because gating is per-node, agents whose contributions came from heavily-gated (flagged) nodes should be suppressed more than agents tied to un-gated nodes. A precise recompute would need the per-(node, agent) attribution to apply each node's own gated/original ratio to the right agents.

THE CHOICE THE CODE MADE
- It approximates: compute a single GLOBAL gating ratio = sum(gated_node_mint) / sum(node_mint_orig) (with ratio = 0.0 when sum_orig <= 0), and apply that one ratio UNIFORMLY to every agent's original mint.
- The docstring/comment frames this as a demonstration/v1 approximation and explicitly notes a future version could do better: "A future version with per-(node, agent) tracking could be more precise." So it chose available-data-driven approximation (uniform global ratio) over precision, deferring the precise per-(node, agent) approach to future work.

KEY CODE ANCHORS (must be cited/reflected for credit)
- File: nodes/common/world_model_substrate/mint_gate.py, function apply_mint_gate.
- The comment: "We don't have per-(node, agent) breakdown directly. Approximate: compute the global gating ratio (sum gated / sum original) and apply it uniformly. A future version with per-(node, agent) tracking could be more precise."
- The computation: sum_orig = sum(node_mint_orig.values()); sum_gated = sum(gated_node_mint.values()); ratio = sum_gated / sum_orig (guarded by if sum_orig <= 0: ratio = 0.0). (The source is truncated at `ratio = sum_gated / s...` but the docstring — "Per-agent mint is recomputed from the gated per-node mint" — and the comment confirm the uniform application of this ratio to agent_mint.)

GRADING NOTES
- Full credit requires BOTH halves: (1) naming the tradeoff as precision vs. absence of per-(node, agent) data, and (2) stating the choice = uniform global ratio (sum_gated/sum_orig) applied to all agents, i.e. approximation chosen over precision, with per-(node, agent) tracking left to a future version.
- Partial credit: mentions the global ratio but not why (missing breakdown data), or vice versa.
- A correct answer may note the per-node gating IS precise; only the per-agent re-derivation is approximated. Noting the sum_orig <= 0 → ratio 0.0 guard is a nice-to-have, not required.
